record.paper_title: A survey on Büchi’s problem: new presentations and open problems
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth projective algebraic surface defined over a number field k. Must there exist a proper Zariski-closed subset Z of X such that every k-rational point of X lies in Z?

evidence.quote: Let X be a smooth projective algebraic surface over a number field k. Does there exist a proper Zariski-closed subset Z of X such that X(k) ⊆ Z?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a number field, and let $X$ be a smooth projective algebraic surface of general type defined over $k$ (i.e., the canonical line bundle $K_X$ is big). Denote by $X(k)$ the set of $k$-rational points of $X$.

Question: Must there exist a proper Zariski-closed subset $Z \subsetneq X$ such that $X(k) \subseteq Z$? Equivalently, is the set $X(k)$ never Zariski-dense in $X$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the surface case of the Bombieri–Lang conjecture, posed by Bombieri in a 1980 Chicago lecture. It remains unproven in general; even for smooth projective surfaces of general type over number fields, no proof of non-Zariski-density of rational points is known. Recent work (e.g., a 2025 arXiv preprint on the geometric Bombieri–Lang) addresses geometric/function-field analogues but not the arithmetic conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Bombieri–Lang conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture asserts that if X is a positive-dimensional algebraic variety of general type defined over a number field k, then the set of k-rational points on X is not Zariski dense.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains unproven in general, including for smooth projective surfaces of general type.

status_evidence.title: The Erdős–Ulam problem, varieties of general type, and the Bombieri–Lang conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Bombieri–Lang for surfaces remains open and would imply Erdős–Ulam.
status_evidence.claim: Surface case of Bombieri–Lang is open.

status_evidence.title: A complete proof of the geometric Bombieri-Lang
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric (function-field) version addressed; arithmetic case over number fields not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Arithmetic Bombieri–Lang for surfaces remains open as of 2025.
